sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Corporate Scope 1-3 Carbon Footprint Auditing and Offset Brokerage

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction for ordinary SARL registration)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China bilateral investment treaty (1984, entered into force 1985)
France-China double taxation avoidance agreement on income and capital (1984, as amended by the 2013 protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq. (as amended); Article L.561-2-2 of the Code monétaire et financier establishing the French beneficial owner register; Code de commerce, Articles R.123-166 et seq.; EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843 as transposed into French law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the beneficial owner's passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the owner's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuer is an Apostille state; otherwise consular legalization by the French Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the owner's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille; consular legalization where Apostille is not applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / registration extract for any corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicable trade or companies registry in the corporate owner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney executed by all proposed shareholders authorizing the French legal representative, with French translation by a sworn translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization with Hague Apostille; for non-Apostille origins, consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners against the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and TRACFIN/ACPR advisories; PEP searches under Article L.561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier; enhanced due diligence on source of funds; ongoing transaction monitoring for identified suspicion indicators.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI, interfaced with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registration documents must be filed in French; a non-French corporate name must be transliterated into Latin characters and, where the source script is non-Latin, accompanied by a French transliteration/translation. The RCS accepts only Latin letters, digits, and a limited set of punctuation marks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be corrected and resubmitted through the Guichet Unique. Within 15 days of a refusal, the applicant may file written observations with the Greffe or petition the juge commis à la surveillance du registre du commerce et des sociétés; further appeal to the Cour d'appel is available within 15 days of the judge's decision. No formal extension of an expired name certificate is available; the applicant must renew the search and obtain a fresh certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed business domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) registered with the local Chamber of Commerce and organized under Articles L.123-11-2 and R.123-136-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. A simple virtual mailbox or PO box is not accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximately 10% within the first 18 months for service-sector SARLs using a shared commercial address, rising to about 20% where the domiciliation address has a history of non-compliance or where the registered activity suggests need for physical substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and certificate of non-registrability (sondage de dénomination / certificat de non-antériorité)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed regulatory tariff for the name search service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed domiciliation agreement for registered office - first quarterly fee/deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-based fee under free competition, subject to registered domiciliation contract

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory legal notice publication in an approved journal d'annonces légales
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Recognized statutory/regulated tariff per line and statutory notice length

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet Unique electronic filing and RCS registration fee (immatriculation principale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / RCS through the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed regulatory filing fee for SARL registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for drafting the statutes (Articles of Association) and compiling the registration file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French business law firm / legal advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for a standard SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO screening and electronic verification per beneficial owner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-owner license and search fee, market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign UBO documents - per document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille authority or French consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official certificate fee plus processing/administrative fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée regime), Article L.223-2 (free determination of share capital), Article L.223-7 (liberation and deposit of cash contributions), Articles L.210-2 to L.210-10 and R.123-230 et seq. (formation formalities and RCS registration); PACTE Law n°2019-486 and Decree n°2021-300 (Guichet Unique electronic filing).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's department, operating the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); filings are submitted exclusively through the INPI Guichet Unique portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise (official form M0 / CERFA n°210113), accompanied by the signed Statuts, certificate of deposit of funds, legal-announcement certificate, and gérant's appointment documents; registration results in issuance of the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for a SARL; founders may fix capital at €1. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation (balance within 5 years), and the corresponding funds must be blocked in a dedicated deposit account (compte bloqué) with a French bank or notaire, released only upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate; capital contributions in kind must be fully transferred at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned associates of SARL [NAME], deliberating as the inaugural general meeting, hereby resolve: 1. Adoption of the articles of association (statuts) establishing a Société à Responsabilité Limitée under Articles L.223-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. 2. Subscription and payment of the share capital of [€X], evidenced by the capital deposit certificate. 3. Establishment of the registered office at [ADDRESS], within the registry district of the relevant Tribunal de Commerce. 4. Appointment of [NAME] as Manager (Gérant), with powers of management and representation. 5. Authorization to deposit funds, publish the legal notice, sign declarations, and execute all formalities for registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés and issuance of the Kbis extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, verification, and signature of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or Notaire (optional); signatures executed either by private deed or notarial act, before a French notary if real estate is contributed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify associate capacities, non-resident shareholding acceptance, and the compatibility of the ESG/carbon accounting corporate purpose with ISIC 7020; draft statutes covering corporate name, registered office, share capital, share transfer restrictions, and gérant powers; secure the registered office's lease or right of occupation; have all associates sign and initial the statutes.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national ID cards of all associates
Utility bill or residential proof (3 months) of each associate
Lease agreement, ownership title, or free-occupation consent for the registered office
Draft Statuts (lawyer-drafted or model form)
Sworn declarations of no criminal conviction and no personal bankruptcy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notaire queries the legal-form clause or corporate-purpose clause, the associates adopt a rectificative resolution and execute an addendum to the statutes prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital into a blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (establishment de crédit agréé) or notaire acting as depositary; Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations as escrow for notarial deposits.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary 'société en formation' account in the company's name; each associate transfers cash contributions (at least 20% of the nominal amount, full capital is market practice); obtain the certificate of deposit of funds (attestation de dépôt de fonds), which lists the subscribers, amounts, and bank or notary references.
required_dossiers: Signed draft Statuts
KYC/beneficial-ownership documents of each subscriber
Company name verification printout (Infogreffe/INPI pre-check)
Identity of the designated Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account opening on AML/KYC grounds, use an alternative licensed bank or a notary's escrow account; the certificate is then issued by the notaire under the same legal effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of a legal notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any legal-announcement newspaper (JAL) approved by the prefecture of the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft notice (avis de constitution) indicating the SARL form, corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, amount of capital, identity of the Gérant, and the RCS registry city; pay the publication fee; retrieve the certificate of publication (attestation de parution) within 1–3 working days.
required_dossiers: Summary sheet of the statutory particulars to be published
Identity details of the Gérant and the registered office address
Attestation de dépôt de fonds (amount to be published)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice for formal defects, correct the text and re-submit; the corrected publication supersedes the defective one, and the registry will accept the latest attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation declaration on the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which transmits the dossier to the Greffe and INSEE.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 creation declaration online, select the SARL legal form, upload the signed Statuts, the capital deposit certificate, the JAL publication certificate, the Gérant's acceptance and identity documents, and the registered office proof; pay the registry taxes online; keep the electronic receipt (récépissé de dépôt) as proof of the filing date.
required_dossiers: Online M0 creation form
Certified copy of the signed Statuts
Attestation de dépôt de fonds issued by the bank or notaire
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Copy of the Gérant's identity document, acceptance letter, and sworn statement of no conviction
Registered office proof: lease, title deed, or landlord's written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique issues a request for completion (demande de complément), cure the missing items within the 15-day legal deadline; the filing is suspended until full compliance, and late reaction triggers a fresh submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance of the complete dossier, the Greffe assigns the RCS registration number, coordinates with INSEE for the SIREN/SIRET codes, and delivers the Kbis extract, which is the sole official proof of legal existence; the company acquires legal personality on this date, and the blocked capital funds are released to the Gérant.
required_dossiers: Complete dossier automatically transmitted by the Guichet Unique
No separate registry application required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed beyond the legal deadlines, file an application before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce in référé; a refusal may be appealed to the court of appeal within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration activation of fiscal and social security accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP (fiscal identification); URSSAF (social security registration of the Gérant and future employees); INSEE (statistical codes); DREETS/DRIEETS (workplace health and safety if hiring).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the SIREN/SIRET assignment and the automatic delivery of the tax identification number; declare the Gérant's social regime (majoritaire/minoritaire) with URSSAF within applicable deadlines; file the DPAE pre-hiring declaration for any first employee; notify the business premises tax (CFE) regime to DGFiP.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Company SIREN/SIRET numbers
Corporate bank account details (RIB)
DPAE form for the first employee, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fiscal or social identifiers are not received within the SLA, contact the competent INSEE/URSSAF unit with the Kbis; late employer registration is corrigible through the self-correction procedure retroactive to the registration date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREALS/DRIEAT (regional environmental directorate, Ministry of Ecological Transition) for environmental oversight; DREETS/DRIEETS for occupational health and safety; ADEME as voluntary supervisory authority for carbon accounting methodologies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific industrial or operational license is mandatory for ISIC 7020 (office-based ESG/carbon consulting and offset brokerage); the RCS registration (Kbis extract) is the sole authorization. Voluntary recognitions include ISO 14064-3 / ISO 14065 validation for audit engagements and ADEME Label Bas-Carbone accreditation for offset project brokerage.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL/DRIEAT – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (Île-de-France: DRIEAT) under the Ministry of Ecological Transition.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Exempt: tertiary office advisory activity is not listed in the threshold-based annex of Article R.122-2 of the French Environment Code and does not fall under ICPE or IOTA nomenclature; no full EIA or prior environmental authorization is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharges: only sanitary water routed to municipal sewerage pursuant to Article R.1331-2 of the Public Health Code; office HVAC systems must comply with F-Gas Regulation (EU) 517/2014; electronic waste (DEEE) must be handled by approved collectors with waste registers under Articles R.541-43 et seq. of the Environment Code; zero-VOC office furnishing and voluntary neutral-carbon electricity contracts are encouraged.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For office premises leased in an existing building, the landlord's fire safety conformity (5th-category ERP) is verified before signature; any premises open to the public above 100 persons require Commission de Sécurité approval (SDIS/managed by the landlord). As an employer, the SARL must obtain an electrical installation conformity certificate (Code du travail Art. R.4214-1 et seq.), undergo workplace health clearance with the occupational health service (médecine du travail/SST), and sign a plan de prévention with co-tenants for shared-site co-activity risks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — official portal impots.gouv.fr; business registration via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; non-resident VAT registration through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and the Direction des Non-Résidents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent must register the French SARL through the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (GFE) to obtain SIREN/SIRET and RCS registration. The GFE transmits the file to DGFiP, which automatically issues the French tax identification number (TIN) and, where applicable, the intra-Community VAT number (numéro TVA intracommunautaire). Non-established foreign suppliers without a French entity must file form SI (TVA) for direct VAT registration with DGFiP and may be required to appoint a tax representative; a TIN for income tax and a VAT number are then issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (French SARL is treated as a company with legal personality; domestic default is partner-level income tax (IR) under CGI art. 8 unless the SARL elects corporate income tax (IS), in which case entity-level taxation applies. For VAT and international treaty purposes the SARL is an entity-level taxpayer.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL may irrevocably elect for corporate income tax (IS) under CGI articles 206(3) and 239; the election is made by the partners, must be notified within the first tax year, and remains binding for five financial years with possible renewal. Family SARLs may continue to be taxed at member level under IR. No US-style 'check-the-box' exists in France; hybrid mismatch alignment is handled through CGI article 205 A and EU ATAD rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) - VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-established suppliers: no general threshold; any first taxable transaction in France triggers VAT registration. Distance sales of goods/e-services within the EU using OSS: €10,000 EU-wide threshold. Domestic small businesses: annual turnover exemption threshold of €91,900 for supplies of goods and €36,800 for services, with optional taxation; this is an exemption threshold, not a registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) and e-reporting of transaction data to DGFiP. From 1 September 2026, all VAT-registered businesses must receive structured e-invoices (EN 16931 / Peppol format) and transmit e-reporting data, either through the public invoicing portal (Portail Public de Facturation - PPF) or a certified private platform (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire - PDP). APIS are used for machine-to-machine exchange with the PPF; transmission is periodic, not real-time, and there is no digital stamping or clearance requirement akin to Italy, Spain, or Latin America.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods from France to destinations outside the EU are taxable at 0% VAT (exemption with credit) under CGI article 262-I-1, provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the EU and supported by commercial documentation. Offshore services, including ESG carbon footprint auditing and carbon offset brokerage, are outside the French VAT territorial scope when supplied under the B2B rule to a taxable person established outside France (CGI art. 259-1); such services are not invoiced with French VAT and input VAT may be recovered under normal deduction rules. If the recipient is established in France or the service is connected to French immovable property, French VAT at 20% applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation) with validated Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR transport document proving physical exit from the EU
Bank transfer / inbound remittance certificate or other irrevocable bank proof of foreign payment
Export Customs Receipt or proof of the goods' arrival in the third country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP scrutinises export zero-rating and offshore service claims through documentary checks and audit procedures. If the export condition or the non-French establishment of the B2B customer is not substantiated, VAT is retroactively re-assessed, input VAT credits are clawed back, and the taxpayer is liable for statutory interest (5% per month) and penalties up to 80% in cases of bad faith (mauvaise foi) and up to 100% for fraud (manœuvres frauduleuses). Criminal fines may also apply for serious evasion, and the six-year ordinary reassessment period applies to missing documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central bank, balance-of-payments and monetary authority), acting with the Direction Générale du Trésor (Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique) as the competent authority for foreign investment screening, and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as banking and KYC supervisory authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is an EU member state; capital movements and payments are fully liberalised within the EU/EEA under Article 63 TFEU and Articles L.151-1 to L.151-4 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF). The euro is freely convertible; France maintains no dual-exchange-rate regime, no approval-based FX allocation, and no statutory distinction between current-account and capital-account transactions for ordinary commercial flows. No exchange licence, economic justification, or prior government approval is required for: (a) subscription and payment of share capital of a French SARL by EU or non-EU shareholders; (b) payment of cross-border advisory invoices or trade disbursements; (c) repatriation of profits, dividends, or liquidation proceeds. The only residual restrictions are: (i) EU/UN sanctions and the French embargo rules applicable to sanctioned jurisdictions and designated persons; (ii) screening of foreign direct investment into France in the 15 strategic sectors extended by Decree No. 2019-1590, which does not capture carbon audit/advisory (ISIC 7020) unless the brokerage arm deals in emissions allowances, which would raise financial-regulation rather than FDI-sensitivity issues; (iii) statistical declaration of cross-border flows to the Banque de France under the balance-of-payments reporting framework and CMF Book V AML obligations imposed on banks. Dividend remittance from a French SARL to a non-resident shareholder is tax-filtered only: a 25% statutory withholding tax applies unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; no central-bank or FX-control approval attaches to such remittance. Conclusion: convertibility is unrestricted for the target entity; the only material compliance hurdle is tax withholding and documentary substance, not exchange control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. France imposes no export-proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory holding or repatriation period for foreign-currency export receipts. The SARL may freely retain USD or other currency proceeds in a foreign-currency account at a French or EU bank, may sell them at market rates, or may use them for settlement, without central-bank authorisation. The only obligations are statistical and AML-related: the enterprise must complete the Banque de France balance-of-payments returns when transaction thresholds are reached (particularly for direct investment flows), and each SWIFT/SEPA wire must carry the appropriate 'nature de transaction' purpose code as advised by the receiving bank. For the carbon-offset brokerage element, the binding constraint is not FX surrender but the AMF/MiFID classification risk: acting as a pure administrative broker for physical carbon credits (no own-account dealing in EUAs, no custody of offset proceeds) is a non-financial commercial activity, whereas dealing in EU Allowances as principal would require AMF/MiFID authorisation and would trigger the securities-reporting framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte bloqué – dépôt de capital) and Operational Account (Compte courant professionnel)
Capital Escrow Account (Compte séquestre) and Operational Account (Compte professionnel)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. (via regional Caisse Régionale)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (Compte courant d'exploitation)
Operational Account (Compte courant) with Capital Escrow Account available on request

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel (Fédération du Crédit Mutuel / CIC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account (Compte professionnel); capital escrow not standard

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for operational cash management, LOW as sole treasury counterparty. ACPR-licensed or EEA-passported electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Revolut Business EU licence, Wise Business) may lawfully hold EUR and execute SEPA CT/SCT Inst and some SWIFT traffic under PSD2, and are efficient for fee collection, expense disbursement, and low-cost FX. However, they are not acceptable as the depositary institution for the statutory share-capital block under Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code (the attestation de dépôt des fonds must come from a bank or notary), may lack a full foreign-correspondent banking network for non-EEA inbound wires, and may not provide the documented Banque de France statistical reporting expected of regulated banks. A non-EEA, offshore-licensed EMI account is generally not viable for the French SARL because it cannot support the French capital-deposit certificate and may raise CRS/FATCA and French tax-residency-evidence complications. Recommended combination: a tier-1 French bank as the anchoring/capital relationship plus a fintech EMI for daily treasury efficiency, with the bank retained for SWIFT-direct global settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SARL whose gérant is a non-resident or lacks a French tax/identity anchor, most tier-1 banks require at least one physical appearance (entretien physique) with the business-opening officer or, alternatively, a certified-identity dossier comprising a notarised passport copy with apostille and a certified proof of address. Pure fully-remote account opening is generally reserved to French-resident gérants with a French ID (passport or titre de séjour) and a French address, which some banks accept via France Identité video verification. EU/EEA passport-holding gérants can usually complete documentary remote onboarding with video KYC where the bank offers it, provided the Registre du Commerce UBO declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif) filed with INPI/RCS is clean and all intermediate shareholders are identified. Non-EEA gérants should budget for an in-branch appointment in Paris, Lyon, or a major regional centre, and for an original or apostilled identity file. The SARL must in all cases present its articles of association, a valid Kbis (unless opening before registration, in which case a draft status plus a signed UBO declaration is used), proof of registered office, and the gérant's proof of identity and address; banks also complete an interview covering source of funds, business plan, and expected volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Articles of association (objet social) containing 'brokerage', 'offset marketplace', or 'trading in carbon credits' language, which triggers suspicion of unlicensed financial intermediation or MiFID activity in emission allowances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rectified objet social limited to 'auditing, consulting, engineering advisory and administrative representation in the voluntary carbon-offset market'; a written legal opinion from a French avocat confirming the company never holds client funds, never takes title to carbon instruments, does not operate a payment account, and acts solely under service contracts with registry-verified offset projects; contractual samples explicitly excluding any dealing on own account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership: non-resident intermediate holding companies or a gérant whose source of wealth and tax residence cannot be verified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial-ownership chain with copies of passports of each individual UBO; apostilled corporate register extracts for each intermediate entity; source-of-wealth letter with three years of bank references; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms (French format n° 5001/5002 or equivalent); personal bank reference letters from an established European bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction exposure in carbon-offset sourcing, particularly where offset registries or counterparties are located in restricted territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening report against the EU consolidated list, UK OFSI, and OFAC SDN list covering all counterparties and counterparty ultimate parents; a written jurisdiction-limitation policy excluding all sanctioned/high-risk territories; contractual carbon-credit provenance register showing serial numbers and registry origin (e.g., Gold Standard, Verra VCS, or equivalent); a forensic AML opinion on each non-standard wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction pattern at opening: large non-resident equity injection followed rapidly by back-to-back outbound wires to third-country suppliers, without a matching commercial explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan and capital-need memorandum matching the statutory capital deposit; signed client and supplier commercial contracts with determined amounts; projected 12-month cash-flow budget aligned with payroll, VAT, and corporate tax cycles; honouring the French doctrine of 'convention courante conclue à des conditions normales' for related-party flows; full invoice and documentary-support file for each outbound disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Advisory-fee receipts structured as 'commissions' on offset trades without commercial substance, which can be misread as layering or as avoidance of MiFID/AMF regulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed fee schedule grounded in audit deliverables (man-days, per-scope reporting, verification preparation) rather than trade volume; time-tracking reports and deliverable evidence; legal memorandum distinguishing administrative brokerage in voluntary carbon credits from dealing in EU Allowances (EUA) as financial instruments under Annex I Section C of MiFID II; signed engagement letters with clients confirming the SARL's role as service provider rather than counterparty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for a non-resident shareholder funding the French SARL: (1) Formation-stage escrow: the gérant selects a French tier-1 depositary bank (or notaire) and requests a 'dossier de dépôt de capital'; the bank opens a blocked fiduciary sub-account in the name of the future SARL under Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code and R.223-3 ff. CMF, representing the capital to be immobilised prior to registration; (2) The shareholder remits EUR via SWIFT MT103 from its own home/corporate bank, quoting in field 50K the remitting legal entity, in field 57A the French depositary bank and its BIC, in field 59 the blocked sub-account IBAN, and in field 70 the advised purpose text: 'Dépôt du capital social – [SARL name] – Article L.223-7 du Code de commerce – [date]'; the receiving bank instructs the correct Banque de France 'nature de transaction' statistical purpose code for a non-resident direct-equity capital inflow (formation de capital / investissement direct entrant) which must be shown on the MT103 and in the bank's BOP return; (3) The depositary bank issues the 'attestation de dépôt des fonds' evidencing the immobilised amount; (4) Following signature of the articles and legal publicity, the RCS registration at INPI (Kbis) is obtained and the bank releases the funds into the SARL's newly opened operational EUR account; (5) The gérant files the UBO declaration, the bank runs the CMF Book V AML checks, and the SARL records the share capital in its opening balance sheet with supporting bank certificate and SWIFT advice; (6) Where the funding is structured as a shareholder loan, the parties execute a written current-account loan agreement with arm's-length interest, and the flow is booked with a corresponding purpose code for intercompany financing; related-party loan agreements with the gérant require compliance with the 'conventions réglementées' procedure of the SARL governance rules to avoid voidability at registration stage.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for the SARL's trade and advisory settlements: (a) EU/EEA supplier payments and refunds: SEPA Credit Transfer (optionally SEPA Instant) using IBAN/BIC under the EPC rulebook, with the VAT reverse-charge accounting file retained for French tax purposes (B2B services); (b) Non-EEA supplier payments, offset-registry settlement, and any non-SEPA disbursement: SWIFT MT103 with documentary support file (invoice, signed contract, delivery/performance proof) and the Banque de France purpose code for commercial service payments; the bank screens each beneficiary against sanctions lists and the SARL should maintain a standing dual-approval treasury matrix; (c) For import of hardware, software, or energy-measurement equipment with meaningful cross-border logistics: commercial letter of credit (UCP600, evidenced by SWIFT MT700) issued/confirmed by a French tier-1 bank, or documentary collection (SWIFT MT400/422) where supplier risk is moderate; (d) Dividends and profit remittances to the non-resident parent: executed via SWIFT MT103 with withholding-tax payment to the French Treasury (Form 2561) and treaty/PDD justification attached to the treasury file; (e) Tax-only disbursements to the French Treasury: SEPA CT referencing the SIRET and tax nature codes; (f) Treasury discipline: all wires matched to approved purchase orders, timely reconciliation against SWIFT FIN acknowledgements, and retention of documentary evidence for the statutory accounting file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD (or EUR/XXX) FX forward (couverture de change à terme) with a French ACPR-authorized bank or EEA investment firm — the standard permitted instrument for locking the EUR equivalent of non-EUR advisory receivables; executed under an ISDA 2002/EMIR-templated confirmation with mandatory trade reporting to an EU trade repository (a French registered TR under EMIR Article 9).

Plain-vanilla FX swap (swap de change) for rolling management of short-term USD/GBP receivables and payables without creating material counterparty risk; subject to the same EMIR reporting, margining and ACPR/ESMA clearing obligations where the counterparty is in the clearing scope; alternatively executed as two matched outright forwards for simplicity.

Cross-currency swap (CCS) for longer-dated multi-year USD-denominated client contracts, fixed-rate to floating-rate or fixed-fixed, matching the SARL's forecast future cash flows; highly restricted to non-financial counterparty threshold and must be cleared through an EU CCP or posted variation margin to a systemic French clearing member; used only where a genuine commercial exposure of substantial duration is documented in the board risk policy.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF): generally NOT available or commercially justified for EUR/USD or EUR/CHF because the euro is freely convertible and an outright forward or FX swap in the liquid interbank market fully covers the exposure; French banks typically refuse NDFs on free-currency pairs for non-financial corporate end-users, and any NDF would be an OTC derivative subject to EMIR clearing/margining where in scope, with trade-reporting obligations — the recommended alternative is an outright deliverable forward.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing at the Trade and Companies Register (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end; shareholders' annual meeting must be held within 6 months, and accounts filed within 1 month thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing triggers a formal notice; if not regularised, the court may impose a fine up to €9,000 on legal representatives and initiate administrative strike-off (radiation) of the company from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats and schedules 2053, 2058, etc.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second working day after 1 May for calendar-year taxpayers; within 3 months of fiscal closing for off-calendar fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers surcharge of 10% (40% if filed within 30 days of formal notice, 80% if not), late payment interest of 0.25% per month, and fixed penalty of €10 for each missing or incorrect schedule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Guichet Unique operated by INPI (for registration with the RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, at the latest concurrently with annual accounts filing (within 7 months of fiscal year-end); any share-transfer-driven change of beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update UBO information: fine up to €7,500 against natural person directors and €75,000 against legal entities; imprisonment up to 6 months for intentional concealment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if for two consecutive fiscal years it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total assets €4,000,000; net turnover €8,000,000; average number of employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG), in line with EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is only permitted for consolidated financial statements of listed groups or specific regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the SARL must verify and confirm through the Guichet Unique that its beneficial ownership data remains accurate and complete. Any share transfer modifying the UBO composition requires supplementary filing within 30 days; the on-site UBO register must reflect the same information as the filed declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shares and securities movements (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of corporate decisions and minutes (registre des décisions d'associés et procès-verbaux)
Register of beneficial owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), kept at the registered office

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $180 – $540 (€150 – €500) depending on location and service provider; Paris premium applies
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,400 – $21,600 (€5,000 – €20,000) for a statutory audit engaged under mandatory thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate; reduced 15% on first €38,120 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first €38,120 of taxable income for companies with turnover < €425,000 and at least 75% individual ownership; research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) available for qualifying R&D and innovation activities; no specific ESG/carbon tax incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (annual corporate income tax return) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr (EFI - Echange de Formulaires Informatisé)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly instalment payments via Form 2571)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is the second business day after 1 May; for other year-ends, within 3 months of fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (bénéfice imposable) after deduction of allowable expenses and depreciation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French-source income only; apply treaty provisions if applicable; attach Form 2065-SD for non-resident companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward (déficits reportables) used to offset current year income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses from French permanent establishment or French-source activities are eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (crédits d'impôt) including CIR, CII, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits directly related to French-source income; attach supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax paid on French-source income (e.g., dividends, interest, royalties)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross amounts and claim treaty relief via Form 5000/5001 if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing documentation declaration (Form 2257) if applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required if related-party transactions exceed €1 million; attach local file and master file if thresholds met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% penalty on tax due if filed within 30 days of deadline; 40% if after 30 days; 80% if fraudulent. Daily interest of 0.20% per month on unpaid tax. Additional penalties for failure to file electronically: €15 per form, minimum €60.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (standard rate; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders; treaty rates typically 15% or 5% for substantial shareholding)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident beneficiary must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from their home tax authority and submit Form 5000 (for dividends, interest, royalties) to the French tax administration before payment. The payer must apply the reduced rate if the TRC is received prior to the payment date; otherwise, the statutory rate is withheld and a refund claim can be filed within the statutory limitation period (typically 3 years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% (reduced to 0% under many treaties, e.g., US-France treaty 0% for certain royalties); Interest: statutory 30% (reduced to 0% under most treaties, e.g., US-France 0% for interest not exceeding arm's length).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1 million in related-party transactions (simplified documentation); full Local File and Master File required if group turnover exceeds EUR 400 million or assets exceed EUR 400 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but requires genuine economic substance for tax residency and treaty benefits. Anti-abuse rules (e.g., Article 155 A of the French Tax Code) target artificial conduit arrangements. A company must have real presence, employees, and decision-making in France to avoid being challenged as a shell company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of taxable income, false accounting, or deliberate misstatement of expenses to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (increased to 7 years for aggravated cases); administrative penalty of 80% of understated tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they participated in fraudulent acts; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices that deviate from arm's length principle, resulting in profit shifting to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty on understated tax (or 80% if deemed abusive), plus interest; potential criminal charges for tax evasion if intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement non-arm's length pricing may face personal liability for penalties and interest; in severe cases, criminal prosecution for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit without real business activity, employees, or premises in France, solely to obtain treaty benefits or avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, 40% penalty for abuse of law (abus de droit), and potential criminal charges for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for taxes and penalties if they knowingly used a shell structure; travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures (e.g., customer due diligence, transaction monitoring) despite being a financial services provider (even low-risk ESG advisory).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million for individuals and €5 million for legal entities; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held criminally liable for AML breaches if they knowingly facilitated money laundering; personal fines and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission or late submission of corporate income tax returns (Form 2065) without reasonable cause.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% penalty if filed within 30 days of deadline; 40% if later; 80% if fraudulent; daily interest of 0.20% per month on unpaid tax; additional fixed penalties for electronic filing non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they intentionally failed to file; in severe cases, criminal prosecution for tax evasion.
